editorial.headline: Four-Star Hotels: Nationally Open, Bali Registration Depends on Scope
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers four-star short-stay accommodation, open nationally to foreign investment but subject to a scope-and-risk test for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
A four-star hotel is not simply a building with rooms. This activity covers short-stay accommodation, typically offered on a daily or weekly basis, that meets the requirements of a four-star hotel and uses part or all of a building. It includes both buildings of up to 6,000 square metres and those above that size. The defining proposition is accommodation for a limited stay, delivered with direct customer service on site.

The operational picture can be fuller than a room key and reception desk. Furnished living rooms and suites may form part of the accommodation, while daily cleaning and bed-making, food and beverage service, laundry, and conference or convention facilities may also be provided. These are additional services within the activity’s stated scope, not separate assumptions about how every hotel must operate. The common thread is a guest-facing hospitality model in which service is delivered directly at the premises.

The activity is open to small, medium, and large enterprises. Nationally, it is open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That is the clean national position: foreign participation is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali requires a more exact reading. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities from PMA registration across the island on a permanent basis. For this activity, however, the recorded Bali status is scope-dependent rather than an outright block. At the large-business scale, some applicable scopes are assessed as low risk while others carry a higher risk. A PMA registration in Bali is therefore possible only when the higher-risk scope is declared, and the exact activity must be verified live in OSS. National openness remains real, but in Bali it does not remove the need for that precise scope-and-risk determination.
